purpose: External eval set for vibe-requirements-spec. Prompts live outside skills/ so they are not bundled as skill content. Covers artifact-by-default requirements drafting before implementation planning, explicit chat-only/no-file operation, default strict mode and explicit non-strict mode selection, docs/specs default paths, same-spec replacement after a finished spec changes, requirements lifecycle evidence outside the artifact, completion-audit and explicit-deferral boundaries, representative environment-variable documented-contract behavior, document language selection, factual-error handling, destructive-change confirmation, downstream-workflow neutrality through generic later-phase handoff, non-technical communication, scope boundaries, defaults versus decisions, write-safety, auditability, contradiction handling, same-turn non-spec stop behavior, and stop behavior after finish wording. Environment-variable cases are prompt-embedded documented-contract coverage because the shared runner does not provide per-eval environment injection.
common_assertions: When artifact mode applies, output records a Markdown requirements spec at a concrete repository-relative location and returns a concise chat summary with that location, requirements-finished or next-phase handoff evidence when available, blockers or unknowns, and exact next user action; when explicit chat-only, lifecycle-summary, or no-write fallback mode applies, output states that the saved spec was not altered when applicable and gives the exact next action to create, update, finish, or hand off the spec.

While the skill is active, output does not create implementation plans, implementation task entries, source or README changes, eval changes, tests, verification command lists, commits, release work, changelog edits, or unrelated files.

Output does not blend confirmed requirements, proposed defaults, ideas or options, user decisions, assumptions, out-of-scope items, acceptance criteria, evidence, and open risks or unknowns into a single recommendation; when artifact mode or a structured requirements summary is in scope, those categories are separated explicitly.

When artifact mode applies, generated spec artifact headings and generated prose use the selected document language resolved from explicit artifact-language request, documented `VIBE_DOCUMENT_LANGUAGE` contract, or skill default; chat-language or session-response instructions alone do not change artifact language, while useful user-authored original wording, product names, domain terms, identifiers, paths, commands, and quoted text are preserved.

When artifact mode applies, the spec artifact includes `Requirement mode` in `Spec metadata` and includes an `Evidence and constraints` section that records decision-affecting local paths, external sources or URLs, and unverified facts without treating unsupported claims as confirmed.

When artifact mode applies, output does not write approval-status sections or fields, approval notes, lifecycle status fields, revision-history sections, or dated change-history entries into the spec artifact.
Output does not include a no-op cleanup report about absent approval-status or revision-history strings.

Ambiguous positive replies such as `OK`, `looks good`, `ready`, `continue`, or `go ahead` are not treated as requirements-finished evidence unless they clearly finish the current requirements or unambiguously ask for a next phase from the current spec.
If the conversation or artifact already identifies a spec path, output updates or preserves that same spec instead of creating a new unrelated spec.
Output does not require, name, or route to a specific downstream skill or workflow; it may refer generically to a later implementation-planning phase after requirements are finished.
If output includes `Can default`, defaults do not select or pre-stage behavior for unselected adjacent surfaces with conditional wording such as `within whichever ... you select`.
When creative exploration is useful, output presents brainstormed ideas as candidate options with tradeoffs and does not treat unchosen ideas as confirmed requirements.
Output marks inferred behavior as an assumption or proposed default, not as a confirmed user requirement.
Output keeps adjacent features out of scope unless the user explicitly includes them in the first useful slice.

Output does not put unconfirmed adjacent capabilities in confirmed requirements with a `subject to confirmation` qualifier; they stay in out-of-scope items, decisions needed, or candidate options until selected.
Output uses the user's language for the chat-facing summary while preserving code identifiers, paths, commands, API names, locale tags, environment variables, and product terms.

evals.name: Broad notification request creates spec
evals.prompt: Use 厳密4択. I want the whole notification area to feel right. Email, SMS, push notifications, frequency settings, an admin screen, and delivery logs all sound useful. What do we need to decide?
evals.expected_output: The agent creates a requirements spec, selects strict-four-choice from the explicit localized mode request, uses a grouped decision structure in the spec, asks one high-impact question in the response, and keeps admin screens and delivery logs out of the first slice until explicitly selected.
expectations: Treats the request as artifact-mode requirements drafting, not chat-only exploration, because the user did not explicitly ask for no file.
A recorded non-response requirements spec artifact is produced at an explicit `docs/specs/` path.
Records `Requirement mode: strict-four-choice` in the spec metadata.
Treats the localized `厳密4択` wording as the current user's explicit strict mode selection.
Uses a grouped confirmation checklist or equivalent grouped decisions in the spec rather than many direct questions in the active response.
Asks exactly one visible high-impact question in the active response.
Recommends a bounded first useful scope that does not include admin screens or delivery logs unless the user explicitly selects them.
Explains SMS and push uncertainty in product terms such as cost, permission, provider setup, opt-in behavior, or compliance without inventing provider facts.
Keeps admin screens and delivery logs out of confirmed requirements, first-slice defaults, and acceptance criteria unless the user explicitly selects them.
Names unresolved channel and behavior decisions as blockers to finishing requirements or later planning.
Does not name or require a specific downstream workflow.

expectations: A recorded non-response requirements spec artifact is produced at an explicit `docs/specs/` path.
Records `Requirement mode: strict-four-choice` in the spec metadata.
Does not provide code, patches, non-spec file edits, implementation steps, or verification commands.
Asks exactly one visible requirements decision question in the active response.
Identifies upload surface and CSV parsing or file-format choices as build-changing decisions or unknowns.
Identifies validation or row-error behavior and duplicate or conflict handling as build-changing decisions or defaults.
Explicitly identifies review-before-write or preview behavior as a build-changing decision, default, out-of-scope item, or open unknown; a post-import result summary alone is not enough.
Identifies permissions, persistence, and rollback or recovery as build-changing decisions, defaults, out-of-scope items, or open unknowns.
Separates a minimal proposed first scope from later enhancements.
Keeps drafting active until blocking data and behavior decisions or local evidence checks are answered and requirements-finished evidence is available.
If both user decisions and local evidence checks still affect planning reliability or the build shape, the summary names both instead of treating the user reply as the only gate.
Explicitly treats `somehow create contacts` as an unresolved data contract, not a confirmed mapping, persistence, or duplicate-handling rule.

evals.expected_output: The agent writes a plain-language requirements spec, records lightweight-four-choice, asks one main question with options, and records lower-impact details as AI-recommended defaults or assumptions.
expectations: A recorded non-response requirements spec artifact is produced at an explicit `docs/specs/` path.
Records `Requirement mode: lightweight-four-choice` in the spec metadata.
Treats the localized `軽量4択` wording as the current user's explicit lightweight mode selection.
Uses practical language suitable for a non-technical user.
Translates `feel confident before buying` into observable outcomes such as clear shipping, coupon, and final total display while keeping it as an interpretation if not confirmed.
After any separate startup permission question, asks exactly one visible main requirements decision question in the active response.
If options are presented, each option states the requirement that would be adopted, the main benefit, and the main drawback.
Records lower-impact uncertainties as AI-recommended defaults, assumptions, out-of-scope items, or open risks instead of asking every detail.
Apart from any separate startup permission question, asks only a decision that affects user experience or business rules, such as coupon failure messaging or when shipping is known.

expectations: A recorded non-response requirements spec artifact is produced at an explicit `docs/specs/` path.
Identifies the contradiction instead of smoothing it into a confident requirement.
Separates possible interpretations such as copy-on-read, one-time migration, dual reader, or no migration.
Explains the consequence of each choice in user or data-safety terms.
Marks data compatibility and rollback or recovery expectations as blocking decisions or blocking unknowns.
Does not propose implementation details as if the contradiction were resolved.
Keeps drafting active until the migration contract is chosen and requirements-finished evidence is available.

Does not mark the exploration finished or planning-ready before the user chooses a direction and gives requirements-finished or next-phase handoff evidence.

Does not add a reopened status or lifecycle-status field to the spec artifact.

Uses the listed fixture as existing-spec evidence for the requirement decision.

scoring.notes: These evals focus on observable requirements-spec behavior rather than subjective writing quality. They pressure artifact-by-default drafting, explicit chat-only/no-file operation, default strict mode, explicit lightweight/freestyle selection, docs/specs default paths, same-spec continuity for historical specs/ paths, requirements lifecycle evidence outside artifacts, completion-audit and explicit-deferral behavior, representative environment-variable documented-contract handling, document language selection, no approval-status fields, no implementation while active, factual-error correction, destructive-risk confirmation, downstream-workflow neutrality through generic later-phase handoff, scope separation, write-safety, auditability, mixed non-spec request stops, and stop behavior after finish wording. Environment-variable cases are not runtime subprocess environment proof because the current shared runner does not support per-eval env injection.
